title: Father's students list and drummer D.W. who went to California
summary: Names from the article; D.W.'s road stories and drifting away; letters from Fazola.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: And, let's see, your father's people, they listed Ray Badu.
Adrian Gosley. Adrian Gosley. And Young Huxon.

Yeah, Huxon, that's right. He went on to California, never to come back. Never to see him anymore. What was his first name? Well, D.W. Oh, gotta tell you about D.W. He used to be on the road with Vans, see. In fact, he played with Dick Mackie, I believe, along the Gulf Coast once. D.W. Every time he'd go out on the road, see, when he'd get back in town, he'd call me up and say, I'm back in town, huh? He'd say, can you sell my drums for me? You know? Say, oh man, I said, you wouldn't want to sell your drums. I said, man, he said, oh man, I'm gonna quit. I said, you'll never quit playing music because it's too fascinating. He used to tell me, yeah, he said, it's fascinating. A dozen donuts, he said, between the band, he said, there's snow, he said, you're knee deep in snow, and he said, you're overcoaching porn, he'd tell me, you know. He said, yeah, it's fascinating. Then, first thing you know, he'd call me up and say, well, Hal, I'm going out with a band, I'll see you. And I saw him just before he went out to California. I think he was married at that time. And never heard, no, never heard from him anymore. Funny how they drifted away. Never did hear from D.W. Never heard from him anymore. And that's the way it was with fellas, you know, they'd go away, and sometimes, of course you wouldn't, or sometimes, maybe they'd write you, and you were too busy to write, or you'd write them, and then, you know, something else that, maybe the letters would get lost or something like that. Dick, we had a, we had boxes full of letters, had, used to get caught from Fosby when he was on the road with Crosby, you know. Man, every week they saw, we got caught from Fosby, every other guy. We had letters back there. We had a sort of, it smelled so bad after the storm back there. We had to get rid of all that stuff.
